CAMPUS PLATFORM • FULL STACK

ClubSphere

ClubSphere is a centralized web platform designed to simplify college club management and improve student engagement. It brings club information, event updates, schedules, and announcements into one accessible place, helping students discover campus activities and stay informed.

Problem Addressed:

College club information can be scattered across different messaging groups and uncoordinated channels. ClubSphere aims to reduce communication gaps, simplify event coordination, and encourage students to participate in campus activities.

Key Highlights & Capabilities:
  • Centralized portal for 6 official college clubs across MLRIT
  • Event discovery for workshops, hackathons, and competitions
  • Announcements and campus notice board with category filters
  • Dedicated club pages and modal registration workflows
  • Organizer authentication and admin dashboard for club leads

UI/UX DESIGN SYSTEM • MOBILE & KIOSK

TEZ Digital Queue System

TEZ is a digital queue system concept designed to eliminate waiting lines (#NO LINE, SAVE TIME). The project presents a structured mobile and kiosk workflow allowing users to choose preferred languages, verify phone numbers via OTP, generate live tokens, view wait status, and consult an AI assistant.

Design Scope:

Presented honestly as a comprehensive UI/UX design prototype in Figma focusing on counter ergonomics and reducing customer anxiety.

Key Capabilities:
  • Multi-language support (English, Hindi, Telugu) with accessibility switch
  • Phone and OTP verification workflow
  • Digital token generation (#PAS-920) and counter routing
  • Integrated AI assistant interface for service guidance

COMMUNITY UTILITY • SUPABASE FULL STACK

Found and Lost

A web platform that helps people report found items and search for belongings they have lost at college events, concerts, and other locations. Users can post information about found items, making it easier for someone searching for a missing belonging to discover it.

Problem Addressed:

Belongings lost at busy college festivals, auditoriums, and crowded events rarely get returned due to lack of a unified registry where finders and seekers can connect.

System Execution Flow • Core Architecture:
[STEP 01]
Item Intake

Users submit lost/found posts with category tags, location metadata, and timestamp details.

[STEP 02]
Supabase Storage

Relational records are stored and indexed in Supabase with real-time status query filters.

[STEP 03]
Instant Retrieval

Seekers filter and match lost belongings by event, hall, and date to claim their valuables.

Technical Implementation:
  • Item submission workflow with detailed descriptions and location tagging
  • Real-time item database backed by Supabase cloud infrastructure
  • Categorized search and filter by date, location, and item category
  • Responsive lightweight user interface deployed on Vercel
HTML CSS JavaScript Supabase Vercel
